Expected: NOT APPLICABLE to this implementation as built. topology-t-model-prototype-spec.md
§4.2/§5.2-§5.3 never creates a real Zabbix Host via LLD host prototypes for an unbound peer —
peers with no matching topo.id/inventory MAC are synthesized in memory at read time only
("d:<key>" node ids), exactly the "rejected sub-variant" topology-tags-use-cases.md §1
describes and explicitly rejects (using A2 as the reason). There is no host-prototype LLD rule
anywhere in this template to test a name collision against. Verdict: BLOCKED, with the reason
being a deliberate design choice, not a gap.
actual: No LLD host-prototype rule exists anywhere in this implementation for peers -- confirmed by inspecting template_topology_discovery_reporter.yaml (only topo.self item + topo.nbr.discovery LLD rule + topo.nbr[] item prototype; no host prototypes at all). There is nothing to collide.
notes: Deliberate design choice (matches the use-case doc's own explicit rejection), not a gap.

expected:
# Q6 — LLD rule returns empty array vs error/unsupported: what happens to existing items?
Expected: an empty array from the LLD rule marks every currently-tracked row "lost" (per the
standard LLD lifecycle) but — because lifetime_type/enabled_lifetime_type are both NEVER
(confirmed live, V2) — none of them get deleted or disabled; they simply stop being
rediscovered. Erroring/throwing from the preprocessing script is a DIFFERENT, worse case this
implementation deliberately avoids: nbr_discovery.js wraps its JSON.parse in try/catch and
returns "[]" on any parse failure rather than ever throwing, specifically so a malformed blob
degrades to "no neighbors this run" instead of an LLD rule error state (whose effect on
existing discovered items is less predictable / template-dependent between Zabbix versions and
wasn't separately verified here). Test: push an empty-neighbors blob to a real reporter,
confirm previously-discovered topo.nbr items survive as `status=0`, un-deleted, un-disabled.
actual: Reproduced cleanly with proper polling (fixed timings, no data loss): after an empty-neighbors push, the item ITSELF stays enabled (item.status=0) and un-deleted (itemDiscovery.ts_delete=0), its own value correctly updates to {"present":false}, and itemDiscovery.status flips 0->1. REFINEMENT to V1/Q2: itemDiscovery.status is exactly the LLD lost/present boolean flag (0=currently discovered, 1=lost) -- it was already in the allowed selectItemDiscovery field list (V1/Q2), just not exercised for its semantic meaning until this test. No topology data or history is erased by an empty LLD result, confirming the expected outcome.

metrics_before.note: see harness transcript: item present:true, itemDiscovery.status=0

metrics_after.note: see harness transcript: item present:false, itemDiscovery.status=1, item.status still 0 (enabled), ts_delete=0
